standard_prerequisites.name: Continuous function on the Cauchy reals
standard_prerequisites.statement: f is continuous when for every u and epsilon there is delta with v close-delta u implying f u close-epsilon f v.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the two moduli theta and eta at source lines 1385-1388.

standard_prerequisites.statement: RC is generated by rational points and limits of Cauchy approximations.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the induction performed at source line 1380.

standard_prerequisites.name: Closeness of limits to the approximating sequence
standard_prerequisites.statement: lim(x) is close to x_delta for small delta.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the retained cited result used at source line 1390 and it is what supplies v.

core_obligations: Prove f(u) = g(u) by induction on u : RC, the rational case being the hypothesis (source lines 1380-1381).
Limit case: assume f(x_delta) = g(x_delta) for all delta and aim for f(lim(x)) close-epsilon g(lim(x)) for all epsilon, so that the path constructor applies (source lines 1382-1383).
Use continuity of f and g to get theta and eta with the two displayed implications (source lines 1385-1388).
Choose delta below min(theta, eta); the retained cited result gives both lim(x) close-theta y_delta and lim(x) close-eta y_delta, so the two displayed implications apply (source lines 1390-1391).
Chain the resulting closenesses through the common value f(y_delta) = g(y_delta) and conclude by the triangle inequality (source lines 1392-1393).

proof_roadmap.step: Induct on the Cauchy reals and reduce the limit case to an epsilon-closeness.
Choose delta, apply the cited closeness and close by the triangle inequality.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 11.3.39 at source lines 1372-1378: two continuous functions on the Cauchy reals that agree at every rational point are equal. The author's proof (source lines 1379-1394) is an induction on the Cauchy reals whose limit case requires assembling three inputs: the two continuity moduli theta and eta obtained from the hypothesis on f and g (lines 1385-1388), a comparison point y_delta which the retained cited result places close to lim(x) within both moduli once delta is chosen small (lines 1390-1391), and the inductive hypothesis f(y_delta) = g(y_delta) inserted in the middle of the chain, after which only the triangle inequality remains (lines 1392-1393). The statement mentions neither the moduli nor the auxiliary point.
